moments.title: Drive to La Fortuna Airbnb
moments.notes:
I expect the rental price to go up with insurance. I don’t expect it to double. Between the customs queue at SJO, finding the Avis shuttle, and sorting out the rental, getting on the road takes some doing. Then we head toward La Fortuna, where a short distance on the map still means a long drive.

Climbing into the mountains around San José, we move through rain, breaks in the rain, and dense fog. We’re genuinely in the clouds. The change from the bottom to the higher stretches is part of what makes the drive so good. Before reaching the Airbnb around eight, we stop for food at a small outdoor restaurant and meet locals who introduce us to Costa Rican moonshine. Not bad, honestly. As a Midwest native, I’ve had homemade grain alcohol that was considerably less convincing.

At the Airbnb, rooms surround a central open air courtyard and pool, with a swing hanging over the water. There are natural wood accents everywhere and a hot tub surrounded by jungle. It’s far enough off the road to feel tucked away. I wish we had more time here. We have just a few hours tonight and the next day to take it in before heading to Bajos del Toro with our guide, Marcos.

moments.title: Bajos Del Toro Remainder
moments.notes:
The highlight of the trip and this was sort of a last minute consideration sobao's Del Toro which is an area not far from La Fortuna has one of the largest density of waterfalls many of them are privately owned on private land quick little hikes but one of them stood out to us Jurassic Canyon it's exactly what it sounds like it's incredible words will not explain especially considering how you have to get there it requires a private guide you park on a Winding Road trust just a random stranger through a power plant and a hole in the fence down a Canyon Ridge down to a riverbed fjording ice cold Rivers the same color as Arctic ice

Jumping gaps between slippery rocks throwing your gear hopefully you don't miss the catch

Passing plants with leaves the side three times your wingspan.

Iconic views and truly real life Cinema the way the Falls reveal themselves to you as you've been trekking. Nothing really would have prepared us for how amazing the experience is going to be.

The majority of the journey isn't bad it's primarily a hike down the first 20 minutes can be a little treacherous especially in when it's wet slippery holding a cable or Vines I would advise you to be mostly capable capable but nothing overly dangerous the Trek back can be a bit physically challenging hiking up the hill but again nothing nothing treacherous and well worth all the effort I plan for at least 6 hours to at least enjoy The full experience and highly highly recommend getting a guide there are no Mark Trails we could easily get lost and being aware of the weather conditions is a must I'll let the videos and photos speak for themselves but truly an amazing experience but this is just one trail of many in the region I'd say skip La Fortuna and spend as much time as you can in Baja del Toro
